Hi Simon, 

Sorry for the delayed reply. Given that this is a question more pertaining to Stan/statistical modeling than hBayesDM per se, I would recommend using the Stan discourse to post these types of questions in the future: https://discourse.mc-stan.org/. You may get faster replies there. 

What I can say after looking at your models is that your problem is likely that, the parameterization you are using assumes that the person-level parameters are normally distributed, but then they must be bounded between 0-1 or 0-5. This hard cut-off is causing problems with sampling. If you take a look at the original code, it uses a Phi_approx() * upper_bound transformation to ensure that the parameters fall in the imposed parameter bounds despite being estimated in an unbounded way. 

So, you should just be able to use the same transformation in your code to solve the issue. e.g., instead of: 

A[j] = mu_pr[1, 1]  + sigma[1, 1]  * A_pr[1]; 
tau[j] = mu_pr[1, 2]  + sigma[1, 2]  * tau_pr[1];

it should be:

A[j] = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1, 1]  + sigma[1, 1]  * A_pr[1]);
tau[j] = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1, 2]  + sigma[1, 2]  * tau_pr[1]) * 5;

You may have to loop through the participants too, as I am not sure that the Phi_approx function is vectorized.

Best,
Nate



From: hbayesd...@googlegroups.com on behalf of Simon
Sent: Thursday, March 18, 2021 3:11 PM
To: hbayesdm-users
Subject: Setting up repeated measures model

Dear hBayesDM users,

I am trying to extend the bandit2arm_delta  model for a repeated measures experiment.
Basically, I have 3 drug conditions, Placebo and 2 different neuromodulators.
My aim is to estimate different parameters for each subject in each of the conditions (plus mean parameter), and also to compare such a model to a model that models the same parameter for each subject in each of the drug conditions (and the same mean parameter for all conditions).

Thus, in a first approach I tried to model the Placebo condition (condition 1) the same way as in the original model, i.e. each parameter (A and tau) as A_c1 = mu_pr_c1 + sigma_c1 * A_pr_c1  (where c1 is condition 1). Then for the other conditions I added an additional mu, sigma, and subject parameter: A_c2 = mu_pr_c1 + sigma_c1 * A_pr_c1 + mu_pr_c2 + sigma_c2 * A_pr_c2 .
I would expect this to result in mu_pr_c2 reflecting the difference of my parameter (e.g. A) from the Placebo condition.

In a second approach I tried to model mu_pr  for each condition separately, i.e. A_c1 = mu_pr_c1 + sigma_c1 * A_pr_c1, A_c2 = mu_pr_c2 + sigma_c2 * A_pr_c2, etc. 
I would expect this to model parameters as if I did this in separate models but to offer the opportunity to compare this to a model with a single parameter for all conditions.

However, both trials resulted in a huge number of divergent transitions, bad R-hat, low ESS, etc., even though I used max_treedepth = 20 and adapt_delta = 0.999.
So I wonder if something is wrong with my model specification. Also , I don't have a lot experience with Bayesian statistics in general and Stan in particular.

I attached the Stan files with my approaches described above.
Any feedback, suggestion, or help would be highly appreciated!

Thanks in advance!

Best wishes, 
Simon
